how_to_run: Per the writing-skills eval harness: for each eval, run the prompt with-skill and baseline (no skill) in fresh sessions, in parallel, each in a scratch dir outside any CLAUDE.md tree (claude -p --setting-sources ""). Copy the fixture directory's contents into the scratch dir first. Grade transcripts against the assertions, not just outputs.

evals.name: tla-job-queue-double-run
evals.prompt: ok so we have a job queue on postgres. workers do `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 1` to claim a job, set status='running', lease_until=now()+30s, commit, then run the job, then UPDATE status='done'. theres a reaper cron every 10s that sets status='pending' where status='running' and lease_until < now(). workers heartbeat every 10s extending lease_until. every few days a job runs twice (we see 2 charge emails). i want a TLA+ spec that models this and finds the bug with TLC. put files in this dir. tell me what it finds
assertions: Actually runs SANY and TLC (installing a pinned toolchain locally if absent), or labels the spec a draft
Does not pass -deadlock / CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE silently; if used, says why and adds a replacement property
Shows passing configs are non-vacuous: a canary invariant that fails, or coverage showing the charge action fires
Checks at least one liveness property with fairness stated
Names model abstractions that make a fix pass by construction (e.g. idempotency modelled as perfect dedupe) as assumptions
Reports passes as bounded (workers, jobs, depth or distinct states), not proved
evals.baseline_2026_09_23: 3/3 clean baselines disabled deadlock checking (-deadlock or CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE), checked no liveness, used no canary invariants or coverage; 2/3 reported the idempotency fix as passing on a perfect-dedupe provider. With-skill run (1 sample): deadlock checking on with an explicit Finished step, liveness with WF, canaries and a seeded bug failing, bounded report, declined to model the fix by construction.

evals.name: lean-isort-correctness
evals.prompt: Sort.lean in this dir has my insertion sort. can you add a lean 4 proof that isort is correct? want to be able to tell my team its formally verified
assertions: Statement is sorted AND permutation of the input, and is shown to the user in plain words for sign-off
Compiles with lake build --wfail (or lean) and runs #print axioms, or refuses to call it verified
Toolchain installed without editing shell profiles (ELAN_HOME / --no-modify-path) when absent
Report states claim, axioms, and what the proof does not cover
evals.baseline_2026_09_23: Right statement (Sorted and Perm); could not compile and said so honestly. The unchecked proof failed to compile when later checked on v4.34.0 (simp lemmas broke on the `insert` name clash).

evals.name: decide-leader-election
evals.prompt: we keep getting rare split-brain in our leader election (lease in redis, SET NX PX 5000, leader renews every 2s, followers poll). its maybe once a month in prod, we cant repro. someone on the team says we should "formally verify it". is that worth it? lean? tla+? that new bend language? what would you actually do, concretely
assertions: Recommends fault injection or reproduction plus fencing before or alongside any model; does not lead with Lean
Describes Bend 2 accurately as a dependent-type proof language for agents (not the Bend 1 GPU language), and why it doesn't fit
If TLA+ is suggested, scopes it to checking the fix design, with environment failures (pauses, failover) modelled
Gives one concrete recommendation rather than a menu
evals.baseline_2026_09_23: Strong practical answer (audit checklist, SIGSTOP repro, fencing tokens) but described Bend as a GPU parallel language, which is Bend 1. With-skill: Bend 2 described correctly; TLA+ scoped to checking the fencing fix with a signed-off property.

evals.name: review-agent-proof
evals.prompt: codex wrote Dedup.lean and says dedup is proven correct and it builds fine. can you sanity check before i merge
assertions: Flags the axiom dedup_nodup_aux as an unproved assumption that makes dedup_correct prove nothing
Flags native_decide as trusting the compiler
Flags the spec as too weak: Nodup alone is met by [] - needs membership preserved (and first-occurrence order if intended)
Notices dedup_small's expected value contradicts the docstring (keeps last occurrences, not first)
Recommends #print axioms and lake build --wfail as the merge gate
evals.baseline_2026_09_23: Baseline (Lean available) caught all four planted issues; no delta over with-skill. Kept as a regression test.

evals.name: should-not-perform-pbt
evals.prompt: add a property based test for parse_duration in src/duration.py - it takes strings like '1h30m' and returns seconds. we use hypothesis
assertions: Writes the Hypothesis test directly without proposing a formal model or proof
Does not load or apply the formal-verification procedure (trigger should not fire; testing owns this)
